resources.string: The selected service has not given any sound yet.
No sound: CDR codes its sound with DRA+, and OnAir does not include a DRA+ decoder (its patent and licence status is unclear). The services, signal information and data work without it.
No sound: the DRA+ add-on cannot be used: %1$s
No services yet: they appear once the multiplex is decoded.
This build has no receiver library, so there is no TV.
Waiting for the transport stream. Start the receiver on a TV channel; the services appear once it locks.
The stream arrives, but no service list yet (PAT, PMT and SDT come within a few seconds).

Picture and sound are decoded by this phone\'s own decoders (Android MediaCodec). OnAir ships no codec: a format the phone has no decoder for stays silent or dark, and the screen says which. Wideband TV demodulation is heavy for a phone: expect it to get warm, drain the battery quickly and, on slower phones, not keep up.
Showing full screen. Back returns here.
Waiting for a picture. Start the receiver on an analogue channel; the picture appears once line and field sync lock.

This is the picture OnAir\'s own analogue receiver makes, the same as on the desktop; the sound comes from the receiver too. No codec is involved. A wide analogue channel is heavy for a phone: expect it to get warm and, on slower phones, not keep up.
OnAir includes no patented codecs and downloads nothing. Build or get a library yourself, copy it to the phone and import it here. It is stored in OnAir\'s own folder.
Where to get it: see docs/CODECS.md. Source: %1$s
This library runs inside OnAir with the same access as the app. Import only files you built yourself or trust. Patent and licence rules are your responsibility.
Imported: %1$s. A library that was already loaded stays until you close and reopen OnAir.
Removing a library that is loaded takes effect when you close and reopen OnAir.
Install the %1$s codec in Settings > Codecs
